WHAT TO BUILD, behind a flag that defaults OFF so nothing changes when it is unset. When a required relation's thing has no holder and its immediate parent entity IS the current scene's location (scene.metadata.location_id), that relation is 'scene-level'. When the flag is on and at least one relation in a verifier request is scene-level, the request state becomes {'narration': text, 'scene': <label of the scene's location>, 'starting_places': {thing name: its place label, for the scene-level relations ONLY}}; otherwise the state is exactly {'narration': text}. The per-relation questions never change. 1) observation.py: ObservedThing gets `scene_level: bool = False` (last field, default keeps old constructions valid); ObservationContext gets `scene: str | None = None` (last field); build_observation_context gets a keyword-only `scene_location_id: str | None = None`; when given, scene = label(world, scene_location_id) (use the same label callable as places), and a visible/contingent thing is scene_level iff holder_id is None and world.parent(entity_id) == scene_location_id. Compare ENTITY IDS, never display strings. prompt_fields output must stay unchanged. 2) observation_verifier.py: Relation gets `scene_level: bool = False` (last); relations_from_context copies ObservedThing.scene_level for unheld things; ObservationVerifier.__init__ gets keyword `scene_state: bool = False`; verify gets keyword-only `scene: str | None = None`; build the state in one small function (`_state_for(narration, relations, scene)`) that returns the J1c state only when self scene_state is on, scene is not None and a relation is scene_level; VerifierReport gets `scene_state: bool = False` (last field) set True exactly when the J1c state was sent. Thresholds, budgets and failure handling unchanged. 3) item_facts.py `_observation_context` passes scene_location_id from the current scene (next scene in self.state.package.scenes whose metadata.scene_id == self.state.current_scene_id). 4) capture.py: both `verify` calls (enforcing in preview_commit, shadow) pass scene=context.scene; if the shadow/enforcing report dicts that capture records list report fields, add a `scene_state` entry next to the others so the enforced run can be read per turn. 5) web_demo.py: constant OBSERVATION_SCENE_STATE_ENV = 'FREYTAG_OBSERVATION_SCENE_STATE'; where the enforcing verifier is built, pass scene_state=(getenv(OBSERVATION_SCENE_STATE_ENV, '') == '1').
